cards.explanation: The answer is that they heard what great things He was doing. Mark says the large crowd came to Him "…when they heard what great things He was doing." (Mark 3:8) Word got around, friends, and I bet nobody needed a group chat to spread it. People came from Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem and more.

The answer is a boat, friends! Jesus asked His disciples to have a boat ready for Him "…so that the crowd would not crush Him." (Mark 3:9) He's standing by the sea, so a boat makes sense. Meanwhile I once got crushed by a pile of takeout menus, and nobody lined up a boat for me.

The answer is touch, friends. Mark says all who had diseases "…were pressing forward to touch Him." (Mark 3:10) He had healed so many that they were pushing in close. That's a lot of folks wanting just one touch.
The answer is "You are the Son of God." The unclean spirits fell down and cried out, "You are the Son of God!" (Mark 3:11) They said it right to His face, friends. They knew exactly who He was.

The answer is False. Mark says Jesus "…warned them sternly not to make Him known." (Mark 3:12) The spirits cried out who He was, but He warned them sternly. I think that's a pretty serious tone, friends, so I'd listen.
The answer is those He wanted. Mark says Jesus "…called for those He wanted, and they came to Him." (Mark 3:13) He picked them, and they came, friends. Nobody had to sign up on a clipboard.

The answers are preach and demons, friends. Jesus appointed the twelve "…to be sent out to preach…" (Mark 3:14) Being sent out to preach is part of why He appointed them, along with being with Him. And He gave them "…authority to drive out demons." (Mark 3:15) The authority came from Him. It wasn't something they cooked up on their own.

The answer is Sons of Thunder. Mark says Jesus named them "Boanerges, meaning 'Sons of Thunder.'" (Mark 3:17) James and John got a name with a boom in it, friends. I'd just ask for a name that sounds good on a cookie box.
The answer is True. Mark closes the list with "…Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus." (Mark 3:19) It's a heavy line to end on, friends. I think this one hurts, so let's just let it sit.
